beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: Christian walked on, still dripping with mud from the Slough. And by the side of the road, a very fine gentleman in a tall black hat was waiting.

beats.speaker: Worldly Wiseman
beats.text: Hello there! You must be Christian from the City of Destruction — the bear with the famous burden!
beats.say: Hello there! You must be Christian, from the City of Destruction. The bear with the famous burden!

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: Famous or not, sir, it is heavy. I'm headed for the Wicket Gate — they say I can be rid of it there.
beats.say: Famous or not, sir, it is heavy. I'm headed for the Wicket Gate. They say I can be rid of it there.

beats.speaker: Worldly Wiseman
beats.text: The Wicket Gate! Dear me. Mud, mountains, lions and worse lie on THAT road. You've already had a taste of the Slough, haven't you?
beats.say: The Wicket Gate! Dear me. Mud, mountains, lions and worse lie on that road. You've already had a taste of the Slough, haven't you?

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: …I'm still drying out, if I'm honest.
beats.say: I'm still drying out, if I'm honest.

beats.speaker: Worldly Wiseman
beats.text: Then listen to a practical bear! In the nearby village of MORALITY lives my good friend Mr. Legality — a master at easing burdens exactly like yours.
beats.say: Then listen to a practical bear! In the nearby village of Morality lives my good friend, Mister Legality. A master at easing burdens exactly like yours.

beats.speaker: Worldly Wiseman
beats.text: A short, SAFE stroll — no mud, no nonsense. You could get a house there, send for your wife and cubs, and live respectably ever after!
beats.say: A short, safe stroll. No mud, no nonsense! You could get a house there, send for your wife and cubs, and live respectably ever after!

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: No mud… a house for my family… Sir, that sounds very sensible indeed. Which way did you say?
beats.say: No mud... a house for my family... Sir, that sounds very sensible indeed. Which way did you say?

beats.speaker: Worldly Wiseman
beats.text: Straight on, past that tall hill. First door on the left! Do give Mr. Legality my regards.
beats.say: Straight on, past that tall hill. First door on the left! Do give Mister Legality my regards.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: So Christian left the true road, and followed the pleasant path toward the village of Morality.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: But the path led right beneath a great, dark mountain… Mount Sinai.
beats.say: But the path led right beneath a great, dark mountain... Mount Sinai.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: At the foot of the mountain, a stone sign said: “Lift your burden by obeying every rule — perfectly.”
beats.say: At the foot of the mountain, a stone sign said: Lift your burden by obeying every rule. Perfectly.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: Perfectly? Perhaps if I try harder than I ever have before…
beats.say: Perfectly? Perhaps if I try harder than I ever have before...

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: No. I have not loved perfectly, spoken perfectly, or obeyed perfectly. I cannot free myself this way.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: The mountain hangs right OVER the road — and fire is flashing from its sides!
beats.say: The mountain hangs right over the road! And fire is flashing from its sides!

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: It shows me everything I have done wrong, but it cannot lift this burden. What have I done?

beats.speaker: Evangelist
beats.text: Christian. What are you doing HERE?
beats.say: Christian. What are you doing here?

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: E-Evangelist! A gentleman told me about a quicker way — a Mr. Legality, who could lift my burden without the mud and the mountains…
beats.say: Evangelist! A gentleman told me about a quicker way. A Mister Legality, who could lift my burden without the mud and the mountains...

beats.speaker: Evangelist
beats.text: Listen carefully, dear bear. That gentleman is Mr. WORLDLY WISEMAN. He loves only the wisdom of this world, and he turns every pilgrim he can away from the true road.
beats.say: Listen carefully, dear bear. That gentleman is Mister Worldly Wiseman. He loves only the wisdom of this world, and he turns every pilgrim he can away from the true road.

beats.speaker: Evangelist
beats.text: Mr. Legality cannot loosen even one strap of your burden. No one has ever been set free at his door.
beats.say: Mister Legality cannot loosen even one strap of your burden. No one has ever been set free at his door.

beats.speaker: Evangelist
beats.text: And THIS mountain is Sinai — the Law itself. It shows your burden for what it is… but it cannot LIFT it.
beats.say: And this mountain is Sinai. The Law itself. It shows your burden for what it is... but it cannot lift it.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: Then I've been a fool twice over — once into the mud, and once onto this path. Is there any hope left for me?
beats.say: Then I've been a fool twice over. Once into the mud, and once onto this path. Is there any hope left for me?

beats.speaker: Evangelist
beats.text: There is. The way you left is exactly where you left it. Go back to the true road, Christian — on to the Wicket Gate — and don't leave it again.
beats.say: There is! The way you left is exactly where you left it. Go back to the true road, Christian. On to the Wicket Gate. And don't leave it again.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: I'll go back at once. Thank you, Evangelist… again.
beats.say: I'll go back at once. Thank you, Evangelist... again.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: So Christian turned around and hurried back to the true road. The Wicket Gate was waiting… but would it open for him?
beats.say: So Christian turned around and hurried back to the true road. The Wicket Gate was waiting... but would it open for him?
